backlog.title: F15 — Community Package-Manager Distribution
backlog.description: Publish every QMKonnect release to native package/version managers users already trust: AUR and Nix flake (Linux), Homebrew (macOS), Scoop and Winget (Windows), plus cross-platform mise/asdf plugins. Each channel honors the per-user, no-admin philosophy where the channel permits. F1-F14 are already fully implemented in the v0.2.8 codebase (390 tests passing); this phase closes the last PRD feature gap (F15).

milestones.title: Linux Community Channels (AUR + Nix)
milestones.description: Create the AUR binary package (qmkonnect-bin) that downloads GitHub release artifacts instead of building from source, and a Nix flake that builds from source with proper Linux dependency integration. Both must install the udev rule, hid-id helper, and systemd service template.

tasks.title: AUR Binary Package (qmkonnect-bin)
tasks.description: Create an AUR `-bin` package that fetches pre-built release artifacts from GitHub instead of building from source. The existing `packaging/linux/arch/PKGBUILD` is a source-build for local makepkg; the AUR package needs a separate PKGBUILD pointing at release tarballs with SHA256 verification.

subtasks.title: Create AUR-adapted PKGBUILD for binary releases
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The existing PKGBUILD at packaging/linux/arch/PKGBUILD builds from source via `cargo build --release` and installs from `target/release/`. It links `-lhidapi-hidraw`. The AUR `-bin` package must instead download the GitHub release tarball `qmkonnect-${pkgver}-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (created by the CI linux-binary job) which contains `qmkonnect`, `qmkonnect-hid-id`, `udev/69-qmkonnect-rawhid.rules`, and `systemd/qmkonnect.service.template`. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §1 for AUR-specific requirements.
2. INPUT: The CI linux-binary job (release.yml lines ~155-185) stages the tarball with this layout: `qmkonnect-{ver}-linux-x86_64/{qmkonnect,qmkonnect-hid-id,udev/69-qmkonnect-rawhid.rules,systemd/qmkonnect.service.template}`. The GitHub release URL pattern is `https://github.com/dabstractor/qmkonnect/releases/download/v${pkgver}/qmkonnect-${pkgver}-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`.
3. LOGIC: Create `packaging/linux/aur/PKGBUILD` with: `pkgname=qmkonnect-bin`, `source=()` pointing at the GitHub release tarball URL, `sha256sums` placeholder (`SKIP` or computed), `arch=('x86_64')`, same `depends`/`install`/`backup`/`options` as the source PKGBUILD. The `package()` function extracts the pre-built binaries and installs them to the same paths (`/usr/bin/qmkonnect`, `/usr/lib/udev/qmkonnect-hid-id`, `/usr/lib/udev/rules.d/69-qmkonnect-rawhid.rules`, `/usr/lib/systemd/user/qmkonnect.service.template`). No `build()` function needed (binary package). Reuse the existing `qmkonnect.install` pacman hooks file (copy or symlink).
4. OUTPUT: `packaging/linux/aur/PKGBUILD` ready for AUR publication.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update packaging/linux/aur/README.md (create if absent) documenting the AUR package, its `-bin` suffix convention, and how to install (`yay -S qmkonnect-bin` or equivalent). This rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: Create .SRCINFO + AUR repo publication infrastructure
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: AUR packages require a `.SRCINFO` file (generated by `makepkg --printsrcinfo > .SRCINFO`) alongside the PKGBUILD. The AUR repo is a git remote at `aur@aur.archlinux.org/qmkonnect-bin.git` containing only PKGBUILD + .SRCINFO + .install. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §1.
2. INPUT: `packaging/linux/aur/PKGBUILD` from P1.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Create `packaging/linux/aur/.SRCINFO` (generated from the S1 PKGBUILD). Create `packaging/linux/aur/publish.sh` — a script that: (a) generates .SRCINFO via `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, (b) commits PKGBUILD + .SRCINFO + qmkonnect.install, (c) pushes to the AUR git remote. The script takes the version as an argument and patches `pkgver` in PKGBUILD before generating .SRCINFO. Document that an SSH deploy key for the AUR account must be configured.
4. OUTPUT: `packaging/linux/aur/.SRCINFO`, `packaging/linux/aur/publish.sh`, ready for CI integration in P1.M5.T1.S1.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add instructions in packaging/linux/aur/README.md for manual AUR publication (the publish.sh script usage). This rides WITH the work.

tasks.title: Nix Flake
tasks.description: Create a Nix flake (`flake.nix` + `flake.lock`) at the repo root that builds QMKonnect from source using `rustPlatform.buildRustPackage`, with proper Linux build dependencies (gtk3, hidapi, libxdo, systemd) and udev/systemd integration.

subtasks.title: Create flake.nix with buildRustPackage + Linux deps
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The PRD says Nix 'builds from source' (§12). The project uses `RUSTFLAGS='-C link-arg=-lhidapi-hidraw'` (PKGBUILD build() and PACKAGING §2). Linux build deps from Cargo.toml `[target.'cfg(target_os = "linux")']`: hyprland (optional), libxdo, tempfile, libc, ksni (optional), gtk (optional). System libs: `libgtk-3-dev libglib2.0-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev libx11-dev libxcb1-dev libxdo-dev libhidapi-dev libudev-dev` (from CI linux-binary job). MSRV 1.88. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §5.
2. INPUT: `Cargo.toml` (for crate metadata, `cargoHash`), `Cargo.lock` (for reproducible builds), `.cargo/config.toml` (Windows CRT-static, not needed for Linux but flake should be cross-platform aware).
3. LOGIC: Create `flake.nix` at repo root with: `inputs.nixpkgs` (unstable or stable), `outputs = { self, nixpkgs, ... }:` producing `packages.{x86_64-linux,aarch64-linux}.qmkonnect` and `packages.{x86_64-linux,aarch64-linux}.default`. Use `rustPlatform.buildRustPackage` with `cargoHash` (or `cargoLock.lockFile`), `nativeBuildInputs = [ pkg-config ]`, `buildInputs = [ gtk3 glib libayatana-appindicator libx11 libxcb xdotool hidapi libusb systemd ]`, and `RUSTFLAGS = "-C link-arg=-lhidapi-hidraw"`. Also build the `qmkonnect-hid-id` binary (it's a separate bin target in the same crate, so it builds automatically). Add `devShells.default` for `nix develop`. Generate `flake.lock` via `nix flake lock`.
4. OUTPUT: `flake.nix` + `flake.lock` at repo root. Users can `nix run github:dabstractor/qmkonnect` or `nix build`.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Create packaging/nix/README.md documenting installation (`nix profile install github:dabstractor/qmkonnect`), the post-install udev/systemd steps (Nix can't install udev rules system-wide), and the `nix develop` shell. This rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: Add udev rule + hid-id + systemd integration to Nix package
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The udev rule (`packaging/linux/udev/69-qmkonnect-rawhid.rules`) references `/usr/lib/udev/qmkonnect-hid-id` (the helper binary). The systemd service template (`packaging/linux/systemd/qmkonnect.service.template`) has `ExecStart=/usr/bin/qmkonnect` and `BindsTo=dev-qmkonnect_device.device`. On NixOS, the system-level udev rule and systemd service need NixOS module integration. On non-NixOS distros using Nix, users install the binary manually and must set up udev/systemd themselves. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §5.
2. INPUT: `flake.nix` from P1.M1.T2.S1, `packaging/linux/udev/69-qmkonnect-rawhid.rules`, `packaging/linux/systemd/qmkonnect.service.template`, `src/bin/hid_id.rs`.
3. LOGIC: In `flake.nix`, add a `postInstall` phase to the `buildRustPackage` that: (a) copies the udev helper `qmkonnect-hid-id` to `$out/lib/udev/`, (b) copies the udev rule to `$out/lib/udev/rules.d/`, (c) copies the systemd template to `$out/lib/systemd/user/`. Additionally create a `nixosModule` output in the flake (a NixOS module that: registers the udev rule via `services.udev.packages`, enables the systemd user service, and adds the user to the `input` group). The module is optional — non-NixOS users just use the binary package and set up udev manually.
4. OUTPUT: Updated `flake.nix` with `postInstall` + `nixosModules.default` output. The package ships all four files (qmkonnect, qmkonnect-hid-id, udev rule, service template).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update packaging/nix/README.md with NixOS module usage (`configuration.nix`: `inputs.qmkonnect.nixosModules.default`) and non-NixOS manual udev setup steps. This rides WITH the work.

milestones.title: macOS Community Channel (Homebrew)
milestones.description: Create a Homebrew Cask for QMKonnect that installs the DMG from GitHub releases. Ship via a custom tap (`brew tap mulletware/qmkonnect`) until notarization qualifies it for the official Homebrew cask repository (PRD §12).

tasks.title: Homebrew Cask Formula
tasks.description: Create the Homebrew Cask Ruby formula that installs QMKonnect.app from the GitHub release DMG, with livecheck for auto-version detection, caveats for Screen Recording permission, and zap for clean uninstall.

subtasks.title: Create Homebrew Cask formula for QMKonnect.app DMG
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The macOS DMG release artifact is named `QMKonnect-{version}-macos.dmg` and contains `QMKonnect.app` (universal binary: aarch64 + x86_64). The bundle identifier is `io.mulletware.qmkonnect`. Screen Recording permission is needed for window titles (PRD §9, PLATFORMS §4.2). PRD §12 says 'Homebrew ships via a custom tap until notarization qualifies it for the official cask.' The DMG is ad-hoc signed unless notarization secrets are set. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §2.
2. INPUT: GitHub release URL pattern: `https://github.com/dabstractor/qmkonnect/releases/download/v{version}/QMKonnect-{version}-macos.dmg`. SHA256 hash of the DMG (computed at release time by CI).
3. LOGIC: Create `packaging/homebrew/Casks/qmkonnect.rb` with: `cask 'qmkonnect' do` block containing `version`, `sha256` (placeholder, updated by CI), `url` (GitHub release DMG), `name 'QMKonnect'`, `desc 'Cross-platform window activity notifier for QMK keyboards'`, `homepage 'https://github.com/dabstractor/qmkonnect'`, `app 'QMKonnect.app'`, `caveats` mentioning Screen Recording permission and the `qmkonnect --show-window-info` discovery tool, `zap trash` for `~/Library/Application Support/QMKonnect/`, and a `livecheck` block using `url "https://github.com/dabstractor/qmkonnect/releases/latest" strategy :header` to auto-detect new versions.
4. OUTPUT: `packaging/homebrew/Casks/qmkonnect.rb` ready for the tap repo.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Create packaging/homebrew/README.md documenting the tap setup (`brew tap mulletware/qmkonnect https://github.com/dabstractor/homebrew-qmkonnect`, `brew install --cask qmkonnect`) and the notarization path to the official cask. This rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: Create Homebrew tap repo structure + update automation
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: A Homebrew tap is a separate GitHub repo named `homebrew-<tapname>` containing a `Casks/` directory. The tap repo is `dabstractor/homebrew-qmkonnect`. Users add it via `brew tap mulletware/qmkonnect`. The tap README needs install instructions and the cask audit steps. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §2.
2. INPUT: `packaging/homebrew/Casks/qmkonnect.rb` from P1.M2.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Create `packaging/homebrew/tap-README.md` — the README.md content for the `homebrew-qmkonnect` tap repo. Create `packaging/homebrew/update-cask.sh` — a script that: (a) downloads the DMG from the GitHub release URL for a given version, (b) computes SHA256, (c) patches `version` and `sha256` in the cask, (d) validates with `brew audit --cask` if available. The script takes version + optional SHA256 as arguments. Document the deploy key needed for CI publishing (P1.M5.T1.S2).
4. OUTPUT: `packaging/homebrew/tap-README.md`, `packaging/homebrew/update-cask.sh`, ready for CI.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] The tap-README.md IS the documentation for this subtask. This rides WITH the work.

milestones.title: Windows Community Channels (Scoop + Winget)
milestones.description: Create the Scoop app manifest (JSON) and Winget package manifest (YAML) for the Windows Inno installer. Both download the `QMKonnect-{version}-windows-x64.exe` release artifact. Scoop ships via a custom bucket; Winget via automated PRs to microsoft/winget-pkgs.

tasks.title: Scoop App Manifest
tasks.description: Create the Scoop JSON manifest for the Inno Setup installer, with checkver/autoupdate for version detection and hash verification.

subtasks.title: Create Scoop app manifest for Inno installer
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The Windows release artifact is `QMKonnect-{version}-windows-x64.exe` (Inno Setup installer, per-user, no admin). It writes HKCU Run autostart, Start Menu shortcuts, and an Add/Remove Programs uninstall entry. The installer exe is not code-signed (PRD §12: 'Scoop unaffected, they don't enforce code-signing'). See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §3.
2. INPUT: GitHub release URL pattern: `https://github.com/dabstractor/qmkonnect/releases/download/v{version}/QMKonnect-{version}-windows-x64.exe`.
3. LOGIC: Create `packaging/scoop/qmkonnect.json` with: `version` (placeholder, updated by CI), `url` (GitHub release installer URL), `hash` (SHA256 placeholder), `innosetup: true` (Scoop detects and runs Inno installers natively), `homepage`, `license`, `checkver` block (`github` source with regex for `v([\d.]+)` tag), `autoupdate` block with `url` and `hash` patterns (hash from the GitHub release `.exe.sha256` sidecar or computed at update time). Add `shortcuts` for Start Menu entry `[['QMKonnect', 'qmkonnect.exe']]` if the Inno installer doesn't create them (it does create Start Menu shortcuts, but Scoop manages its own shortcuts).
4. OUTPUT: `packaging/scoop/qmkonnect.json` ready for the bucket repo.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Create packaging/scoop/README.md documenting the bucket setup (`scoop bucket add qmkonnect https://github.com/dabstractor/scoop-qmkonnect`, `scoop install qmkonnect`). This rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: Create Scoop bucket repo structure + autoupdate config
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: A Scoop bucket is a separate GitHub repo containing a `bucket/` directory with JSON manifest files. The bucket repo is `dabstractor/scoop-qmkonnect`. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §3.
2. INPUT: `packaging/scoop/qmkonnect.json` from P1.M3.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Create `packaging/scoop/bucket-README.md` (README for the bucket repo) and `packaging/scoop/update-manifest.ps1` — a PowerShell script that: (a) downloads the installer from the release URL for a given version, (b) computes SHA256 (`Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256`), (c) patches `version` and `hash` in the manifest JSON, (d) optionally validates with `scoop checkup`. Document the deploy key for CI publishing.
4. OUTPUT: `packaging/scoop/bucket-README.md`, `packaging/scoop/update-manifest.ps1`, ready for CI.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] The bucket-README.md IS the documentation. This rides WITH the work.

tasks.title: Winget Package Manifest
tasks.description: Create the Winget package manifest (YAML) for the Inno Setup installer, with automated PR submission to microsoft/winget-pkgs on each release.

subtasks.title: Create Winget package manifest (YAML)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Winget manifests are YAML files. The modern manifest format (v1.6+) uses a single `*.yaml` file or a multi-file directory. The PackageIdentifier is `dabstractor.QMKonnect`. The installer is Inno Setup type (`InstallerType: inno`), per-user scope (`Scope: user`). PRD §12 says Winget prompts 'unverified publisher' (unsigned). See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §4.
2. INPUT: GitHub release URL: `https://github.com/dabstractor/qmkonnect/releases/download/v{version}/QMKonnect-{version}-windows-x64.exe`. Inno installer details: per-user, `{localappdata}\Programs\QMKonnect`, HKCU Run autostart, Start Menu shortcuts.
3. LOGIC: Create `packaging/winget/dabstractor.QMKonnect.yaml` with: `PackageIdentifier: dabstractor.QMKonnect`, `PackageVersion` (placeholder, updated by CI), `DefaultLocale: en-US`, `ManifestType: merged` (single-file format) OR separate `*.installer.yaml` + `*.defaultLocale.yaml` + `*.version.yaml` files. The installer entry: `InstallerType: inno`, `InstallerUrl`, `InstallerSha256` (placeholder), `Architecture: x64`, `Scope: user`, `InstallModes: [interactive, silent]`, `InstallerSwitches: { Silent: /VERYSILENT, SilentWithProgress: /SILENT }`. Package metadata: `Publisher: Mulletware`, `PackageName: QMKonnect`, `License: MIT`, `Homepage`, `ShortDescription`, `Tags: [qmk, keyboard, hid, tray]`. Add `ReleaseDate`, `UpgradeBehavior: install`.
4. OUTPUT: `packaging/winget/dabstractor.QMKonnect.yaml` (or directory of manifests) ready for wingetcreate.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Create packaging/winget/README.md documenting the Winget installation (`winget install dabstractor.QMKonnect`), the 'unverified publisher' warning, and how the automated PR workflow works. This rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: Create Winget publishing automation via wingetcreate
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Winget packages are published via PRs to `microsoft/winget-pkgs`. The `wingetcreate` CLI tool can automate this: `wingetcreate update dabstractor.QMKonnect --version {ver} --urls {url} --token {GITHUB_TOKEN}`. Alternatively, the `vedantmgoyal9/winget-pkgs-automation` GitHub Action watches for new releases and submits PRs automatically. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §4.
2. INPUT: `packaging/winget/dabstractor.QMKonnect.yaml` from P1.M3.T2.S1.
3. LOGIC: Create `packaging/winget/submit.ps1` — a PowerShell script that: (a) downloads the installer for a given version, (b) computes SHA256, (c) runs `wingetcreate update dabstractor.QMKonnect --version {ver} --urls {installer_url}|{sha256} --submit --token {token}` (or generates the manifest locally without `--submit` for review). Document the GitHub PAT requirement (needs `public_repo` scope for winget-pkgs PR). Also document the alternative: add this repo to the `vedantmgoyal9/winget-releaser` action in CI.
4. OUTPUT: `packaging/winget/submit.ps1`, ready for CI integration in P1.M5.T2.S1.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add a section in packaging/winget/README.md on the submission workflow and PAT requirements. This rides WITH the work.

milestones.title: Cross-Platform Version Managers (mise + asdf)
milestones.description: Create an asdf plugin that mise can also use directly (mise is asdf-compatible). The plugin downloads the appropriate pre-built release binary for the user's OS/arch and installs it into the version manager's prefix. This covers both mise and asdf from a single plugin.

tasks.title: asdf Plugin (compatible with mise)
tasks.description: Create the asdf plugin shell scripts (bin/install, bin/list-all, bin/download) and document mise compatibility. The plugin lives in a separate repo `dabstractor/asdf-qmkonnect` but the scripts are staged in `packaging/asdf/` in this repo for CI to publish.

subtasks.title: Create asdf plugin scripts (install, list-all, download)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: asdf plugins are shell-script based, living in a separate repo named `asdf-{toolname}`. The three required scripts are: `bin/list-all` (prints available versions), `bin/download` (fetches the release artifact for a given version + OS/arch), `bin/install` (extracts to `$ASDF_INSTALL_PATH`). Release artifacts per platform: macOS=`QMKonnect-{ver}-macos.dmg` (need to extract .app from DMG), Windows=`QMKonnect-{ver}-windows-x64.exe`, Linux=`qmkonnect-{ver}-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (contains qmkonnect + qmkonnect-hid-id + udev + systemd). mise is fully asdf-compatible: `mise plugin add qmkonnet https://github.com/dabstractor/asdf-qmkonnect` works without any plugin changes. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §6-7.
2. INPUT: GitHub Releases API: `https://api.github.com/repos/dabstractor/qmkonnect/releases` for version listing. Release artifact naming patterns (from CI release.yml): macOS DMG, Windows exe, Linux tarball.
3. LOGIC: Create `packaging/asdf/bin/list-all` — scrapes GitHub API for tags, prints space-separated versions. Create `packaging/asdf/bin/download` — maps `uname -s`/`uname -m` to artifact name, downloads via `curl`, validates SHA256 if sidecar exists. Create `packaging/asdf/bin/install` — extracts the platform-appropriate artifact to `$ASDF_INSTALL_PATH/bin/` (Linux: tar extract; macOS: mount DMG + copy qmkonnect binary from the .app bundle; note: the raw binary works for CLI but not menu-bar without the bundle context — document this caveat). Also create `packaging/asdf/lib/utils.bash` for shared helper functions.
4. OUTPUT: `packaging/asdf/bin/{list-all,download,install}`, `packaging/asdf/lib/utils.bash`.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Create packaging/asdf/README.md (the plugin repo README) documenting: asdf setup (`asdf plugin add qmkonnect https://github.com/dabstractor/asdf-qmkonnect`, `asdf install qmkonnect latest`, `asdf global qmkonnect latest`), mise setup (`mise plugin add qmkonnect ...`, `mise install qmkonnect@latest`), and the macOS caveat that the raw binary lacks bundle context for the menu-bar icon. This rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: Create asdf plugin repo metadata + mise native backend stub
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: asdf plugins need a `.tool-versions` example and optionally a `mise.toml` for mise-native support. While mise can use asdf plugins directly, a `mise.toml` in the plugin repo enables mise-specific features. The plugin also needs a `CHANGELOG.md` and a GitHub Actions workflow for testing. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §6-7.
2. INPUT: `packaging/asdf/bin/*` from P1.M4.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Create `packaging/asdf/.tool-versions` example (`qmkonnect 0.2.8`). Create `packaging/asdf/mise.toml` with `[tools]` section documenting the asdf-compat path. Create `packaging/asdf/publish.sh` — a script that clones the `asdf-qmkonnect` repo, copies the bin/ scripts + lib/ + README, commits, and pushes (used by CI in P1.M5.T2.S2). The script requires an SSH deploy key for the asdf plugin repo.
4. OUTPUT: `packaging/asdf/.tool-versions`, `packaging/asdf/mise.toml`, `packaging/asdf/publish.sh`.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] The mise.toml and .tool-versions ARE documentation for version pinning. This rides WITH the work.

milestones.title: CI Pipeline Integration
milestones.description: Add publishing jobs to the existing `.github/workflows/release.yml` so each tag push automatically updates the AUR package, Homebrew tap, Scoop bucket, and Winget manifest. Add validation for the Nix flake and asdf plugin.

tasks.title: AUR + Homebrew + Scoop CI Publishing Jobs
tasks.description: Add three new jobs to release.yml that publish the updated PKGBUILD, Homebrew cask, and Scoop manifest to their respective external repos after the GitHub Release is published.

subtasks.title: Add AUR publication CI job
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The existing release.yml has a `publish` job that creates the GitHub Release. The AUR job must run AFTER publish (needs the release artifacts live). It needs an SSH deploy key for `aur@aur.archlinux.org`. The version is already extracted in earlier jobs. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §1.
2. INPUT: `packaging/linux/aur/publish.sh` from P1.M1.T1.S2. The GitHub release URL for the Linux tarball.
3. LOGIC: Add a new `aur` job to `.github/workflows/release.yml` that: (a) runs `needs: [publish]` and `if: github.event_name == 'push'` (tag only), (b) configures SSH with the AUR deploy key (from secrets), (c) clones the AUR repo `ssh://aur@aur.archlinux.org/qmkonnect-bin.git`, (d) runs `publish.sh {version}` to patch pkgver, generate .SRCINFO, copy files, (e) commits and pushes. Add `AUR_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY` to required secrets documentation.
4. OUTPUT: Updated `.github/workflows/release.yml` with the `aur` job.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Document the `AUR_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY` secret requirement in a comment block in the release.yml job. This rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: Add Homebrew tap + Scoop bucket publication CI jobs
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Both the Homebrew tap (`homebrew-qmkonnect`) and Scoop bucket (`scoop-qmkonnect`) are external repos that need git pushes with deploy keys. The Homebrew cask needs the DMG SHA256; the Scoop manifest needs the installer SHA256. Both can be computed from the downloaded artifacts or from GitHub release asset checksums. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §2-3.
2. INPUT: `packaging/homebrew/update-cask.sh` from P1.M2.T1.S2, `packaging/scoop/update-manifest.ps1` from P1.M3.T1.S2.
3. LOGIC: Add two new jobs to release.yml: (1) `homebrew-tap` job (runs-on ubuntu, needs publish, configures SSH deploy key for `github.com/dabstractor/homebrew-qmkonnect.git`, clones the tap repo, downloads the DMG to compute SHA256, runs `update-cask.sh {version} {sha256}`, commits and pushes). (2) `scoop-bucket` job (runs-on windows or ubuntu, needs publish, configures git token for `github.com/dabstractor/scoop-qmkonnect.git`, clones the bucket repo, downloads the exe to compute SHA256, patches the JSON manifest with version + hash, commits and pushes). CONTRACT DEFINITION:

Alternatively, use `wingetcreate` directly in a CI job. The PAT needs `public_repo` scope. See plan/007_fb356ba503b4/architecture/external_deps.md §4.

This action automatically finds the installer in the GitHub Release, computes the hash, and submits a PR to winget-pkgs. Alternatively, if using submit.ps1: run it on windows-latest with wingetcreate installed.
